newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TAYLOR SHUNS CAUTION AGAINST WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR SHUNS CAUTION AGAINST WEST INDIES.

text.p: Australia head into the third test against West Indies on Thursday needing only to avoid defeat to retain the Frank Worrell trophy but captain Mark Taylor has rejected any thought of playing for a draw.

Australia, who beat West Indies in the Caribbean last year, lead the current five-test series 2-0, leaving the tourists with the daunting task of needing to win the remaining three test matches to reclaim the trophy.
But Taylor adopted a positive approach on the eve of the traditional Boxing Day test match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
"The last thing I want from any side is to go into a test looking to draw it. Five days is a long time to head for a draw from the word go and teams that do that often end up losing," Taylor said.
The left-handed New South Wales opener praised his side's consistency in thrashing West Indies in Brisbane and Sydney.
"The great thing I saw about this Australian team in the first two tests is that we didn't just play one good day and hold on, we played five good, solid days," Taylor said.

West Indies, who reversed a dismal run of form with convincing wins in a limited overs match against Pakistan and a first-class fixture against Victoria, are considering promoting wicketkeeper Junior Murray to opener.
Team manager Clive Lloyd said Murray could move ahead of specialist openers, Robert Samuels and Adrian Griffith, who have both struggled for runs on tour.
West Indies have enjoyed a timely boost with the return to form of fast bowler Ian Bishop and key batsmen Sherwin Campbell and vice-captain Brian Lara against Victoria.
Despite their comfortable victories in the first two tests, Australia have changed their batting line-up, dropping number three Ricky Ponting and recalling left-hander Justin Langer.
Opener Matthew Hayden was also called up as a replacement for fellow opener Matthew Elliott, who suffered a serious knee injury while batting in the second test.
Australia will also be boosted by the return of veteran all-rounder Steve Waugh, who missed the second test because of a groin strain.

Australia (from) - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Hayden, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Justin Langer, Michael Bevan, Greg Blewett, Ian Healy (vice-captain), Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Jason Gillespie, Glenn McGrath

West Indies (from) - Sherwin Campbell, Robert Samuels, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Junior Murray, Courtney Browne, Ian Bishop, Curtly Ambrose, Kenny Benjamin, Courtney Walsh (captain), Nixon McLean.
